alerts.title: Renal function monitoring needed on TDF with hypertension and proteinuria
alerts.message: Guidelines require eGFR monitoring for TDF at 3 months, 6 months, then 6-12 monthly, with high-risk patients (co-existent hypertension or diabetes) needing closer monitoring. Patient has hypertension (146/94), trace proteinuria, regular ibuprofen (NSAID) use, and on TDF. Creatinine 112 umol/L is within normal limits, but eGFR is not recorded and the plan does not specify renal monitoring frequency. Serum phosphate is low (0.78 mmol/L), which may reflect TDF-associated proximal tubulopathy, though this is not explicitly addressed in the guideline excerpts provided. Non-drug causes of proteinuria (hypertensive nephropathy) remain plausible.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR today and monitor renal function at 3 and 6 months then 6-12 monthly. Avoid TDF if eGFR <50 mL/min/1.73m2. Consider urinalysis/proteinuria follow-up and reassess NSAID use given renal risk.

alerts.title: Amlodipine non-adherence and peripheral oedema-related monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines advise observing amlodipine side effects such as lower limb oedema and considering alternatives if persistent. Patient reports heavy-feeling thighs and stiff gait, with no pedal oedema noted today. Patient misses amlodipine doses during transit, contributing to suboptimal BP control (146/94). The clinician plan refills amlodipine but does not address adherence strategies or BP target re-evaluation.

evidence.recommended_action: Address adherence barriers during transit; reassess BP control at follow-up and monitor for amlodipine side effects such as lower limb oedema, considering alternatives if excessive or persistent.
